AI Notes.value: GTF is an established London graphic design studio founded in 1990 by RCA graduates Paul Neale, Nigel Robinson, and Andy Stevens; Robinson left in 1993 and was succeeded by Huw Morgan. Currently ~11 people: three principals/creative directors (Neale, Stevens, Morgan) plus a fourth creative director (Robbie Mahoney), five designers, and two ops staff. Senior / studio-director level, 35+ years of practice; considered one of the most influential British graphic design studios. Clients include Frieze (9-year identity relationship), M&S, Science Museum, Vitra, Kvadrat, Gagosian, Design Museum; 2008 Art Institute of Chicago retrospective was the museum first ever solo show for a single graphic design studio. Work spans graphic design, identity systems, wayfinding (Vitra, M&S), and exhibition design (Science Museum); studio profile explicitly names exhibition design, environmental design, and wayfinding as disciplines. Autonomy 5: fully independent studio, co-owned by three principals, no parent company. Work Status Studio confirmed from site and all sources.
